stories.headline: Millions strike across Spain over soaring rents
body: Millions of Spanish workers walked out on Wednesday, shutting businesses and transport over rents and housing prices.
It was Spain's first general strike in 14 years, and the first driven mainly by housing.
A national election is due later this month.
stories.joke: When rent costs more than your salary, the strike plans itself.
stories.vc: Pressure for rent rules could hit property investors and landlords in Spain.

stories.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases
body: Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 11,000 cases, the government said.
5,387 people have died, nearly half of those infected.
It is the country's deadliest outbreak, declared in mid-May.
stories.vc: Outbreaks this size strain aid budgets and slow trade and mining in the region.

stories.headline: Iran says Hormuz will never go back to pre-war rules
body: Iran's top negotiator Ghalibaf says the Strait of Hormuz will never return to its pre-war status.
He says Iran and Oman have agreed to oversee the waterway, as part of Iran's seven-point peace plan.
Iran is waiting for a formal US reply.
stories.vc: New rules over Hormuz could permanently raise shipping costs for oil importers like India.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps 773 points as foreign money flows in
body: The Sensex rose 773 points (0.95%) to 81,879, and the Nifty gained 0.84% to 25,255.
Foreign buying, strong results and softer oil prices helped.
Mahindra & Mahindra led with a 5% jump.
stories.joke: The market is back to its favourite exercise: going up.
stories.vc: Steady foreign inflows support the rupee and IPO pipeline.

stories.headline: Diwali smartphone sales fall up to 20% as prices rise
body: Phone shops sold 18-20% fewer phones over the five-day Diwali period, retailers' body AIMRA says.
Sales value held steady because phones cost more.
Memory chips are going to AI servers, pushing phone prices up.
stories.joke: AI ate your new phone's memory chip.
stories.vc: Rising part costs could squeeze phone makers' margins and offline retailers.

stories.headline: India bans export of lithium battery 'black mass'
body: India has barred exports of lithium-ion battery waste containing 'black mass'.
Black mass is the powder of lithium, nickel, cobalt and graphite left after recycling batteries.
The aim is to keep these minerals in India for EVs and electronics.
stories.joke: Even battery dust is now too valuable to export.
stories.vc: The ban is a boost for India's battery recycling startups.

stories.headline: OpenAI's quarterly revenue tops $10B for the first time
body: OpenAI's revenue passed $10 billion in a quarter for the first time, Bloomberg reports.
That is almost 50% more than the $6.7 billion reported for the second quarter.
Its operating losses also narrowed.
stories.joke: $10 billion in a quarter, and still not profitable. Classic AI.
stories.vc: Faster growth strengthens OpenAI's case for a possible 2027 IPO.

image.credit: European Commission - Photographer: Aurore Martignoni / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Unhedged: can Nvidia's board rein in Jensen Huang?
body: The FT's Unhedged says the Huang affair scandal has wiped billions off Nvidia's value.
It asks whether a board with no chair and no succession plan can control its CEO.
Congress also plans to call Huang to answer questions.
stories.vc: Weak governance at the world's most important chipmaker is a risk for the whole AI trade.

stories.headline: UK chip startup Fractile raises $720M
body: British AI chip startup Fractile raised a $720 million Series C, backed by the UK's Sovereign AI Fund.
It builds chips and software to run AI models faster and cheaper.
It is now one of the best-funded AI chip startups.
stories.joke: Britain wants its own chips. And not the fried kind.
stories.vc: Governments funding chip startups shows AI hardware is now a national priority.

stories.headline: CoreWeave asks customers to pay upfront to fund AI growth
body: CoreWeave's revenue rose 168% to $3.66 billion, but it lost $709 million.
It now asks customers to prepay and uses shorter contracts.
It paid $846 million in interest last quarter.
stories.vc: If AI demand cools, firms like CoreWeave carrying heavy debt are most at risk.

stories.statLabel: of US VC money to first-time funds
stories.headline: First-time VC funds face their worst year in a decade
body: First-time funds got just 4.5% of US venture fundraising this year, PitchBook says.
Established firms on their fourth fund or later took 88%.
Olaf Sakkers of RedBlue Capital is trying to beat the squeeze.
stories.joke: Venture capital: it's who you know, and how long you've known them.
stories.vc: Fewer new funds means fewer backers for unusual early-stage startups.

stories.statLabel: top Seneca posts held by women
stories.headline: Tina Abrams sworn in as Seneca Nation's first woman president
body: Tina Abrams was sworn in as the Seneca Nation's first elected woman president.
All three of the nation's elected executive posts are now held by women.
She pledged to keep defending the nation's sovereignty.
stories.vc: Tribal leaders control big gaming and land businesses, so leadership changes matter economically.

stories.headline: Cornell faces another sexual assault lawsuit
body: A newly uncovered 2023 lawsuit says Cornell's Title IX office ignored repeated sexual assault complaints.
Two female students say the same male student assaulted them.
The case may go to trial next year.
stories.vc: Lawsuits like this push universities to spend more on handling complaints properly.

stories.headline: Supreme Court gives Centre more time on Delhi women's safety plan
body: The Supreme Court extended the Centre's deadline to 23 November in its own case on women's safety in Delhi.
The case began after a series of rapes in Delhi-NCR.
The government says it wants a plan that can work across the country.
stories.vc: Safer public spaces help more women take up jobs, a big boost for India's workforce.

stories.headline: CCI clears Advent's ₹3,150 crore bet on Yatharth Hospitals
body: The competition regulator approved Advent International's ₹3,150 crore investment in Yatharth Hospitals.
Advent will hold a minority stake of 24.9%.
The money will fund Yatharth's hospital expansion across India.
stories.vc: Big private equity cheques show investors expect strong growth in India's hospital sector.

stories.headline: New AIIMS hospitals pass 6 crore outpatient visits
body: The new AIIMS hospitals have recorded over 6 crore OPD consultations since 2021-22.
Yearly visits rose from 50 lakh to nearly 1.45 crore in 2025-26.
18 of the 22 new AIIMS approved are fully functional.
stories.vc: More regional AIIMS reduce the need to travel to Delhi for advanced care.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu to create 4 regional directors for its medical colleges
body: Tamil Nadu will create four Regional Directors of Medical Education and Research posts.
The state now has only one director, in Chennai, for its growing number of medical colleges.
The minister also opened a new photopheresis unit at the children's hospital in Chennai.
stories.vc: Better oversight of public medical colleges improves training and hospital services across the state.

stories.statLabel: Mercedes' engine gap to Red Bull Ford
stories.headline: FIA's final engine review keeps Red Bull Ford as the benchmark
body: The FIA's final 2026 review of its engine catch-up rules (ADUO) found no change.
Red Bull Ford remains the benchmark, so it gets no extra upgrades.
Ferrari, Audi and Honda, over 4% behind, keep their two extra upgrades for 2027.
stories.joke: Best engine, no upgrades. Winning has its penalties.
stories.vc: Catch-up rules shape how much makers spend on engines, and who wins in 2027.
